quest.title: Qiaoying, the Village of Many Tales
quest.description: You once again meet the slightly paranoid author, Guijarro, in Qiaoying Village...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x3

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: ...This cat... Of course, that has to be it! Great, I just knew it!

choices.text: Guijarro?

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: #Huh? {NICKNAME}, Paimon, imagine running into you here! What're you doing in Qiaoying Village?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Have you... finished writing your book? You wouldn't still happen to be imagining weird things, would you?

choices.text: Or having symptoms of paranoia?

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Oh, no, no! I've already finished writing that book. Right now, it's just a matter of waiting for "The Courtcraft of Fontaine" to get printed and go on sale.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, Paimon's hooked just hearing the title! What's the book about?

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Let's see... it's about a cowardly detective and his fearless little sister, who's also acting as his assistant. They come across a "Crime Museum," which hosts within it the evidence for countless crimes...

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Throughout the story, they also encounter missing twins, a meka puppet that cries, and a museum curator who's been drowned in his fountain... and in the end, they find out that the prime suspect is none other than a child who just turned three years old!

choices.text: Okay, enough of that! I'm getting chills!

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Hahaha! Once it officially goes on sale, I'll send you both autographed copies.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Score! But... Paimon might be too scared to read it on her own...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #It's decided then! {NICKNAME}, please read it to Paimon!

choices.text: I—I'm also too scared...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really...? Then it looks like our only choice is to read it together!

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Come on, you two. No need to ham it up like that. It's just a crime novel, not a horror story.

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: As for something truly terrifying... I plan on writing a new novel. I've already made a rough outline, and I've been looking everywhere for new material to use as inspiration for the details.

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: ...Hey, don't look at me like that! This time, all I want to do is combine the crime novel with some local folk tales. Even if we're collecting reference materials, there's no way I'll be all paranoid and jumpy like before.

choices.text: Why not do this in Fontaine?

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Ah, well... You see, many people have already written about Fontainian folklore, and I want to write something... a bit more original!

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: It also just so happened that a friend of mine was planning to come here to check out the tea business, so I tagged along.

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: No sooner had I stepped off the boat than I discovered some truly stellar subject matter! Just as I was considering how to best pursue the matter, you two came over.

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: To borrow the local Liyue lingo, this would be... uh, um... "destined to meet, though originally separated by more than a thousand miles"?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Already adapting to the local culture, I see...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How should Paimon put it... Well, maybe it's no wonder you're a great writer? You're so quick when it comes to understanding the local customs...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But did you just say you've already found something? There's nothing here!

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Says who? Look! Do you not see this cat?

choices.text: Seen it from the start! But what's so strange about a cat?

response.speaker: Confused Kitty
response.text: Meow...? Meeeow...

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Ah, you must be unaware. In the legends of Qiaoying Village, there are strange beasts known as "Xuanwen Beasts."

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: According to the legends, these strange beasts appear like young cats and can sense good and evil, concealing themselves at night and rising with the sun, eating... uh... eating the wind and drinking the dew, crossing a thousand miles in a day, and gnawing tea trees at night to nourish themselves...

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Anyway! That's what the article in "Bedazzled!" said, at least!

choices.text: You can tell from the name it's a load of tripe!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Feels like whoever wrote that... All they heard was the name "Xuanwen beast," and they just tossed every weird rumor they'd ever heard into a pot and started stirring!

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Still, based on my own investigations, there are indeed "Xuanwen beasts" near Qiaoying Village, even if I'm still a bit fuzzy on the details... But as long as they exist, then I can study and use them!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow! Guijarro's completely different from before. She used to be so scared and timid...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And now, she came all the way here with nothing but a name to go on...

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Hahaha! Apologies! It's one of my faults. As soon as I start writing, I'll find myself drawn into the same mindset as the book's characters.

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: The protagonist of this book is a super-confident detective! So self-assured that you could say they consider everyone else to be beneath them...

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Alrighty! That's enough blah-blah for now. I need to carefully research this little...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The cat turns and flees like lightning...

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Whoa! It ran away, after it!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Without another word, Guijarro breaks into a run, sprinting after the cat at breakneck speed...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not again! We've gotta catch up to her quickly, or who knows what kind of wacky hijinks Guijarro will get up to this time!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Guijarro! Not so fast!

choices.text: Where did you dig up a tabloid like that?
Unless... it isn't a cat, and is instead...?

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: You think so too!? I knew it, haha, great minds always think alike!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nononono! Not at all! No matter what, it looks like it's just an ordinary little kitty!

choices.text: You came all the way to Qiaoying Village just to get some reference material...

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: After all, Fontaine's folk tales have been written to death! I just want to write something original.

choices.text: Leave it to me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! You're the best.

choices.text: Sounds like quite the case...
We're not in Fontaine anymore. You're quite a ways from home.
Is there... something wrong with this cat?

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: #Ah, I believe it is... Eh? Huh? {NICKNAME}, Paimon, imagine running into you here! What are you doing in Qiaoying Village?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...See? Paimon said it was just an ordinary kitten.

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: Huh. To think that...

dialogues.speaker: Confused Kitty
dialogues.text: Meow? Meow... meow, meow?

choices.text: Do you know of any Xuanwen beasts?

response.speaker: Confused Kitty
response.text: Meow...?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The cat turns and leaves, looking frustrated...

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Still... Do you think that this kitten could be the young form of the mythical beast, lying low here in Qiaoying Village till it is fully grown, and can destroy all the tea trees in one fell swoop...

response.speaker: Hung Fan
response.text: Ms. Guijarro, not this again... Anyway, haven't I told you before that Xuanwen beasts are hardly that gentle?

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Ah, Ms. Hung Fan! What a coincidence. What brings you here today?

response.speaker: Hung Fan
response.text: *sigh* Please stop mentioning things like "criminal cases" around here — what if the children begin to take you seriously?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You know each other?

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Yes. When I came here, it was this lady who I hired to help me carry my baggage. I also consulted her regarding all manners of folklore.

response.speaker: Hung Fan
response.text: If I've told you once, I've told you countless times that Xuanwen beasts won't appear here, but you just won't believe me. What was that thing you said...

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Even if they won't appear, I'll still have many ways to collect information on them.

response.speaker: Hung Fan
response.text: There you go again... I know my hopes of dissuading you were slim, but still, I must ask you not to leave the village willy-nilly.

response.speaker: Hung Fan
response.text: The beasts are actually quite dangerous, so if you do end up encountering one... *sigh* Anyway, please do not leave the village on your own!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Hung Fan leaves, looking even more exhausted and resigned than the cat from earlier...

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Well, since Ms. Hung Fan said so, we're going to have to go elsewhere to get our material. Come then, follow me.

choices.text: Sorry, we've got the wrong cat.

response.speaker: Confused Kitty
response.text: Meow...

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: What do you think? This...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A tea cauldron.

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: That's right, and it does... something with the tea... that makes it kinda special... Whatever the case, it's been placed smack dab in the middle of this place, too! If you ask me, it must hold some special significance.

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: Hmmm. Now then, what if... our Xuanwen Beast has been using this as its hiding place all along?

choices.text: You'll be writing a fantasy story at this rate, you know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Feels like the next thing you know, you'll introduce some Adepti into the story...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I dunno if that's the right kind of plot to write for a crime story...

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: ...Hmm, those are some fine expressions you've got there. Are you thinking, perhaps, that a crime story centered around a Xuanwen beast might feel too "absurd" to be taken seriously?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, uh, yeah, kinda? Can you really use something like that to move the plot forward?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait, don't tell me you're...

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: #Haha, aren't you a sharp one, {NICKNAME}? You sure do live up to your fame.

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Exactly! I intend to write about a "crime too absurd to be possible." Your reactions, along with Ms. Hung Fan's, are very interesting. I'll include them into my novel for sure.

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: As for the Xuanwen beast... It shall be my "perpetrator." A creature that has never been seen, but is said to devour the village's evil-doers.

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: During a certain festival, a villager is found to have met their end at the hands of some wild beast outside the settlement...

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: But during the second festival day, the main character encounters the victim, who should be dead — only for yet another victim to soon emerge afterward...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, and then what? Then what!

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Well, I haven't thought that far yet.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...I'm leaving now.

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Oh, come on! Once I finish, I'll send you two autographed copies for sure. In fact, I've still got a big favor I'll need your help with!

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Ms. Hung Fan has said that I shouldn't leave the village by myself, right? Well, I've taken her advice to heart!

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: But... now that you're here, I'm no longer alone! That means I can go outside!

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: We're not going to go too far off, of course! So, are you willing to help me out?

choices.text: Well, sure... We'll do it so you can tell us the end of your story.

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Well, then! Let's head over there, shall we? There's a place I'd like to go!

choices.text: Please follow the standardized payment model, thanks.

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Of course. Don't you worry!

choices.text: I don't think this is a crime story anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: So these are "lanterns"? These ones look like fish — how very fascinating!

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: So these handles can be used to raise the lanterns up? Hmm... With this detachable structure, someone with a head for engineering design can easily have a section or two secretly added without being discovered...

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: The space within is pretty large. You should be able to insert a few...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Stop! Jolly well keep those thoughts to yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: Eh? Oh... Right! Hahaha, sorry. I just can't stop myself from thinking aloud upon seeing these fascinating things...

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: Hmm. Yes, I'm sure of it — the addition of "lanterns" will add much to my novel.

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: Could I trouble you to go to the side, and take a picture of this "fish lantern" for me? I'd like to have a reference picture for later.

choices.text: Well, time to hone my Kamera skills some more, I guess...

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: I'm leaving the photo-taking in your hands, then... Ah, yes. Please make sure you'll grab a shot of the entire lantern — this is incredibly important to me!

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: ...Cooking up a scheme related to "dimensions" will be quite interesting... The question now is how they will solve the weight problem...

choices.text: Leave it to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Where did Guijarro go? Wasn't she here just a moment ago?

choices.text: Guess she was kidnapped by a Xuanwen beast?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, don't say stuff like that! She probably just ran off somewhere thinking about her plotline. Let's search the area.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The tea field to the side gives us a good vantage point. Let's start from there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good idea! Let's start our search from up high!

choices.text: Did her novel turn out to be truer than fiction?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guijarro! How did you get over here?

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: ...No, no. I can't have them find the key clue just like that. Also, can someone really still think well after being tied up here all night?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, she's totally engrossed. Has she finally found a breakthrough?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: More like a real roadblock.

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, you've arrived just in time.

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: Could you tie me to a wooden stake?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: D—Did Paimon hear that right?

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: Yep, that's exactly what I said. Please tie my hands, and string me up by them on a... tree. Um, well, they're all wood anyway, so it should make no difference.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't intend to become the suspect in your novel.

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: Oh, don't worry, I've already written up a liability document, which assigns responsibility for all mishaps that might occur to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, no, that's not the problem. Why do you want us to tie you up at all? You haven't done anything wrong...

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: But the main character of my novel will be strung up by their hands by the villagers and left in the wild for a whole night, awaiting the Xuanwen beast's judgment.

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: Later in the plot, the main character, having expected this turn of events, will somehow survive, and endure the night, before revealing the truth behind everything...

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: ...However, I have no clue how a person who has been tied up for a whole night would feel. Not how they'd sound, think, or even move!

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: That's why I need you two to tie me up and keep me here the whole night. That way, I'll be able to experience those feelings for myself.

choices.text: Nope. This is way too dangerous.

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: ...Um. Well, there is, but it probably wouldn't be as effective.

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Instead of that, I could... raise my hands up and stay here for the whole night.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Or you could just not write that novel. Our actions here could be easily misunderstood...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're really putting your main character through the wringer...

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Please! This is the most important step! Once I get over this hurdle, my novel will be complete! If we use this method, you won't have to commit any crimes...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not that we ever had to!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We never had to in the first place!

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Ah... Well, I mean, you really don't have to do all that much. Just stand guard by my side so that I won't be dragged off by someone... or some animal, while I gather the information I need.

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Let me see... Considering the atmosphere we're trying to create in the novel, we still need to go further up...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Hey! Wait for us!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You and Guijarro climb to the highest point of the tea fields...

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Whew, I—It's... kinda c—cold, but it... really gets you into the mood of things!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you really going to stand here the whole night with your hands upraised?

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: That's right. I've decided to do this. Some sacrifices must be made for the sake of writing...

response.speaker: Guijarro
response.text: Well, please stand guard here in the meantime. Just one night... Just one night...

choices.text: Isn't there a safer way to do this?

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: ...Don't think the character would be able to return to the village alone like this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guijarro!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's help her up first...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You help Guijarro up so she's sitting properly on the ground.

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: So that's how it feels... It's quite awful, indeed. Not only am I exhausted... I feel like even my mind's gotten all sluggish...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mission accomplished, then?

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: Of course. I finally know how it feels to be tied, strung up, and left to the elements for a night.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That protagonist of yours is pretty tough...

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: That's right. I've also figured out how the protagonist is going to chase the Xuanwen Beast away. If we conclude the story that way, it will surely... Surely...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh? Are they going to pull off a super cool trick?

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: It will surely... be really awesome...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Guijarro faints once again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Hey! Guijarro, you...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Couldn't you have said how this would work *before* fainting?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A—Anyway, let's get her to a doctor... Back to the village!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ms. Hung Fan was right. This lady really shouldn't have left the village...

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: The scheme won't quite work with just these lanterns... What should I do...

dialogues.speaker: Guijarro
dialogues.text: Let me think... How exactly should I raise my hands? Hmm...
